request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, administered by Intersect for the vendor
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Mithril Protocol continuous development through the Intersect budget process

claims.claim: The proposal requests 3,810,423 ada, consisting of 3,699,440 ada for Mithril Protocol Continuous Development and 110,983 ada for an Intersect Budget Administration fee.

Mithril is described as using stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify Cardano state in a trustless way so nodes and applications can verify state rapidly without relying on the entire chain.
The proposal says Mithril addresses slow full-node synchronization and centralized-trust dependence by improving secure access to and verification of blockchain state.
The proposal states that funding Mithril through Intersect MBO supports Cardano scaling while preserving decentralization guarantees and reducing dependency on centralized indexers and hosted APIs.
The proposal claims it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and references external voting and audit materials.
The proposal claims the requested amount did not, at time of submission, breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713, and links to the relevant governance action.

The proposal states that audit and oversight costs are included in the overhead and that independent oversight will be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.

The document states that Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs, but has contributed to Mithril for several years through IOG-funded collaboration.

The proposal says Intersect will administer funds using Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts, with listed TRSC and PSSC addresses, specified multi-party authorization thresholds, and an external Oversight Committee of six named entities.
The proposal references a public dashboard and on-chain smart contract framework for community auditability of the withdrawn ada and related metrics.

summary: The document requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development, administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts with oversight arrangements, but it provides only a high-level budget and lacks detailed feasibility, risk, alternatives, failure-mode, and milestone information in the supplied text.
